entries.meaning: A fictional blend of Xavier and Thanatos, associated with new house and death.
entries.meaningEvidence: Supplied literary blend; component associations do not imply a traditional inherited name.
entries.note: A male given name used in modern fiction.
entries.sourceEtymology: A blend of Xavier + Thanatos originally coined by the creators of the television show Gargoyles, and subsequently used by other authors in their own fiction.

entries.meaning: From Ancient Greek Ξανθή (Xanthḗ, literally “blond-haired”), from ξανθός (xanthós, “yellow”).
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek.

entries.meaningEvidence: Conventional Basque etxe plus berri through the place name Xabier.
entries.note: A male given name from Spanish [in turn from Basque].
entries.sourceEtymology: Toponymic surname of a 16th-century saint born in the Kingdom of Navarre, Francis de Xavier, from a place name in the Kingdom of Navarre, originally from Basque Xabier. Doublet of Echeverría.
entries.sourceProvider: Kins AI-assisted interpretation; Wiktionary etymology reference

entries.meaning: Possibly related to Xenia, associated with hospitality.
entries.meaningEvidence: Possibly variant of Xenia, Greek xenía (“hospitable”); origin qualified.
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek of modern usage.
entries.sourceEtymology: Possibly a variant of Xenia, from Latin Xenia, from Ancient Greek ξενία (xenía, “hospitable”), the assumed name of a fifth-century saint venerated in the Eastern Orthodox Church, from ξένος (xénos, “foreign, strange”).
entries.sourceProvider: English Wiktionary contributors; Kins sourced summary

entries.meaning: From the assumed name of a fifth-century saint venerated in the Eastern Orthodox Church, Latin Xenia, from Ancient Greek ξενία (xenía, “hospitable”). Doublet of Oksana.
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek of mainly historical use in English.
entries.origin: Ancient Greek of mainly historical use in English

entries.meaning: From Ancient Greek Ξενοφάνης (Xenophánēs). The name means “of foreign appearance” and is composed of ξένος (xénos, “foreign”) + φαίνω (phaínō, “appear”).
From Ancient Greek Ξέρξης (Xérxēs), from Old Persian 𐎧𐏁𐎹𐎠𐎼𐏁𐎠 (x-š-y-a-r-š-a /⁠Xšayāršā⁠/, “ruler among kings”). Doublet of Ahasuerus.
entries.note: A male given name from Old Persian mainly applied to historical and fictional characters.
entries.origin: Old Persian mainly applied to historical and fictional characters

entries.meaning: Can suggest dawn and cleverness, or little and cleverness, depending on the Chinese characters.
entries.meaningEvidence: Supplied source gives Xiaomin as either Xiaomin with dawn or little character plus clever.
entries.note: A female given name from Mandarin.
entries.sourceEtymology: Borrowed from Mandarin 晓敏 (Xiǎomǐn), probably originally 小敏 (Xiǎomǐn), diminutive of 敏 (Mǐn).
